text:
maria: Heads-up — we just saw a corrected ECC spike on gpu-pool-eu-045. Error rate jumped ~10x in the last 30m, scheduler started moving pods off a couple of cards. Sample from dmesg: 

[maria] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=23456, GPU=0 
[maria] nvidia-smi -q -d ECC 
[maria] ===============
[maria] GPU 0 ECC errors (corrected): 124 total (since boot)
[maria] GPU 1 ECC errors (corrected): 7 total

maria: Noticed GPU0 is the hot one; load looks normal otherwise. Opening thread to decide threshold/next action.

kai: thanks for flagging. Is this repeat on that host or new?

maria: first time we've seen that magnitude on this host in last 30 days. Historical sliding window shows mostly zeros then this spike.

sophie: can you paste pod list on that node + any recent model loads? maybe a large context job triggered a kernel path?

maria: pods on node: model-ingest-1, rtrank-worker-3, analysis-batch-7. Nothing unusual. No recent driver restarts.

anil: if it's corrected ECC only, our usual flow is: 1) soft-quarantine the card (stop scheduling new workloads), 2) monitor for uncorrected/Xid fatal escalation, 3) if continues escalate to drain+replacement. Proposal: soft-evict threshold = >100 corrected errors in 1h OR >300 in 24h.

ben: +1 to soft-first. Question: do we soft-quarantine at card granularity or whole node? Kubernetes doesn't natively do card-level drains. We currently mark node unsched and let pods be rescheduled. That wastes healthy cards on node.

sophie: we have device-plugin label trick — annotate the GPU as "rotating=true" and update scheduler to avoid new allocations to that index. Ops script can patch daemonset to remove device from allocation pool.

maria: here's a runbook snippet I'm typing up for this thread: 

1) quick triage: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `journalctl -u nvidia-driver | grep -i xid` 
2) if corrected-only and below hard-fail thresholds -> mark card quarantined: `kubectl annotate node/gpu-node-045 gpu-quarantine=gpu0` and update device-plugin config to hide device
3) watch for 2 windows (30m each) of continued increases -> if rises -> escalate to `kubectl drain` node and RMA card
4) collect `dmesg`, nvml logs, and upload to support ticket (attach GPU UUID, driver version, firmware)

kai: sounds good. For automation, can we change alerting to look at per-card corrected-rate with hysteresis? e.g., trigger soft-quarantine only after crossing 100 corrected errors in an hour AND still >120 after a 20m recheck. That reduces noisy flips.

anil: agree on hysteresis. Also add cooldown: once we auto-quarantine a card, ignore further auto actions for 24h unless uncorrected/Xid severity increases.

ben: we should avoid aggressive hard-drain for multi-tenant nodes during peak hours. Suggest schedule-only soft actions between 00:00-08:00 UTC for full drains. Immediate hard-drain only for uncorrectable or Xid=79/43 series (fatal).

sophie: note: driver 525.89 had a known corrected-ECC regression on some Tesla cards — do we have this node pinned to that driver? Maria?

maria: node is on 525.105. No known regression recorded for that exact minor, but we'll add driver version to diagnostic output.

james: ops-bot created incident INC-20260318-42 and attached initial logs. Ops-bot: please run automated collection script `scripts/gpu-collect --node gpu-node-045 --gpus 0` and upload.

ops-bot: ACK INC-20260318-42. Started collection job, ETA ~3m. :gear:

maria: after soft-quarantine we saw corrected errors drop to 6 in 30m for GPU1 but GPU0 stayed hot (added 60 more corrected). So far no uncorrectable.

kai: Given persistence, suggestion for automation change: implement card-level state machine: OK -> WARN -> QUARANTINED -> REPLACE. Transitions: OK->WARN at >30 corrected/hr, WARN->QUARANTINED at >100 corrected/hr sustained across two windows. Add manual override. Store history per-GPU UUID.

anil: and tie cost control: when quarantining many cards in a pool, autoscaler should spin up new nodes in dedicated pool if free capacity low. Prevents throttling production jobs.

ben: also add a metric-based eviction cap: at most 1 GPU (or 25% of GPUs) can be quarantined per-node per 24h automatically to avoid cluster churn.

sophie: I'll draft the heuristic doc and open a PR in infra-alerts; will include sample queries: 
`sum(rate(gpu_ecc_corrected_total{region="eu-west-1",gpu_uuid!=""}[1h])) by (gpu_uuid)` 
`gpu_ecc_corrected_total - increases per GPU over window`

maria: next steps: I will soft-quarantine GPU0 and monitor 2h, attach logs to INC-20260318-42, and then we can merge Sophie’s PR for alert changes if it matches this flow.

anil: agreed. Also let's schedule a short postmortem if the card ends up RMA — include kernel, driver, firmware, workload characteristics.

ben: thanks team. If you need a quick script to patch device-plugin, ping me.

maria: doing the patch now. Will update thread with results in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
